chunks: What Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿUrwah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, from one of the two of them, peace be upon them, concerning:
the urine of riding animals touching the garment, so he disliked it. I said: Are not their meats halal (permissible)? He said: Yes, but they are not among those which Allah has made for eating.
So this report came as a clear explanation of all these reports, explicitly stating the karāhah of what they contain.

key_terms.أَبْوَالِ: urine; here, the excretion whose contact with clothing is being discussed
key_terms.الثَّوْبَ: the garment or clothing affected by impurity or disliked matter
key_terms.الدَّوَابِّ: riding animals or beasts of burden
key_terms.حَلَالًا: halal (permissible); referring here to the legal permissibility of meat
key_terms.كَرَاهَةِ: dislikedness; the legal sense explicitly indicated in the report
key_terms.لِلْأَكْلِ: for eating; indicating animals designated for consumption
key_terms.مُفَسِّرًا: explaining or clarifying; describing this report's function toward other narrations

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the urine of riding animals if it touches one's clothing?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling concerning the urine of riding animals when it comes into contact with clothing. Although the meat of such animals may be described as halal in one sense, the narration clarifies that they were not created for consumption, and thus the report indicates karāhah regarding what was mentioned.
